claims.locator: widely reported attribution, not repudiated by Davis; Mitchell estate provenance
claims.sourceText: Widely reported 'Wilson-Davis memo'; Davis has not publicly repudiated authorship. Primary provenance is the Mitchell estate, not a government release.
claims.text: Notes attributed to Davis of a 16 October 2002 meeting with Vice Adm. Thomas R. Wilson, former Director of the DIA, describe a special access programme within a defence contractor that refused Wilson access; the notes surfaced in 2019 among the estate papers of Apollo astronaut Edgar Mitchell.

claims.sourceText: The Wilson-Davis notes, 16 Oct 2002, as circulated from 2019
claims.text: The notes record Wilson describing being refused access, on need-to-know grounds, to a special access programme holding recovered non-human material in contractor custody.

claims.sourceText: Notes attributed to Eric W. Davis of a 16 October 2002 meeting; circulated publicly from 2019
claims.text: The Wilson-Davis memorandum records Adm. Thomas Wilson being denied access to a special access program holding a recovered craft, on the basis that the program sat with a private aerospace contractor and he had no need to know.

claims.sourceText: The Wilson-Davis notes as published, fifteen pages, read image by image, https://documents2.theblackvault.com/casefiles/wilsonleak.pdf
claims.text: The published document is typed, not handwritten, and two of its fifteen pages are somebody else's letter. The copy in public circulation is fifteen typed pages headed 'EWD NOTES', then '10/16/02', then 'Eric Davis Meeting with Adm. Wilson', numbered 1 to 15 at the foot. Pages 3 and 4 are a two page letter on United States Navy letterhead dated April 25, 2002, from Belleair Bluffs, Florida, to 'Dr. Eric W. Davis, CEO, Warp Drive Metrics', signed 'Will Miller'; the notes flag it at the foot of page 2 as '[paper-clipped letter here]'.

claims.sourceText: The Wilson-Davis notes as published, all fifteen pages, https://documents2.theblackvault.com/casefiles/wilsonleak.pdf
claims.text: Brig. Gen. Steven Lovekin is not in the published notes. All fifteen pages were read image by image: Wilson, Davis, Steven Greer, Will Miller and Edgar Mitchell are in them and Lovekin is not.

claims.sourceText: The Wilson-Davis notes as published, pp. 3 to 4, https://documents2.theblackvault.com/casefiles/wilsonleak.pdf
claims.text: The notes give the correspondent no rank, no service and no first name beyond 'Will', and his letter carries no rank block, so the 'Cdr. Willard Miller, USN' form used across the podcast corpus is not supported by the document it is drawn from. In the letter he writes: 'Although I have held a Top Secret (TS) clearance with access to Special Compartmented Information (SCI), and other "special" clearances for "other" programs, I currently do not work in the classified realm, nor do I hold those clearances.'

claims.sourceText: The Wilson-Davis notes, 16 Oct 2002, in public circulation since 2019
claims.text: The notes record Wilson describing a 1997 attempt to gain access to a special access programme holding recovered non-human material in contractor custody, and being refused on need-to-know grounds by a programme security officer, a contractor programme manager and a lawyer.

The Davis notes record Wilson stating he was refused access to a special access programme holding recovered non-human material, on the grounds that he lacked need-to-know, despite his position as Joint Staff J-2.

claims.sourceText: The Wilson-Davis notes as published, pp 3-4, https://documents2.theblackvault.com/casefiles/wilsonleak.pdf
claims.text: The published Wilson-Davis notes reproduce, as their pages 3 and 4, a letter on United States Navy letterhead dated April 25, 2002, from Belleair Bluffs, Florida, to 'Dr. Eric W. Davis, CEO, Warp Drive Metrics', signed 'Will Miller', offering assistance 'with your ongoing research into UFO crash retrievals and the entities within the government (or outside of it) that are involved in that business'.

claims.sourceText: The Wilson-Davis notes as published, p 4, https://documents2.theblackvault.com/casefiles/wilsonleak.pdf
claims.text: In the same letter Miller writes: 'Although I have held a Top Secret (TS) clearance with access to Special Compartmented Information (SCI), and other "special" clearances for "other" programs, I currently do not work in the classified realm, nor do I hold those clearances.'

claims.sourceText: The Wilson-Davis notes as published, pp 5-6, https://documents2.theblackvault.com/casefiles/wilsonleak.pdf
claims.text: The notes record Wilson as 'Very furious - very angry about Miller' for having 'Violated personal and professional trust - especially among intelligence colleagues/Navy officers', and carry Davis's own parenthesis that 'Miller told Ed Mitchell who only told me in 1999'.

claims.sourceText: The Wilson-Davis notes as published, p 1, https://documents2.theblackvault.com/casefiles/wilsonleak.pdf
claims.text: The notes record Wilson confirming that 'Greer/Miller/Mitchell gave talk in Pentagon Conference room' in April 1997 with Adm. Mike Crawford and Gen. Pat Hughes present, and that afterwards 'Miller/Wilson talked (privately) 2 hours on UFOs, MJ-12, Roswell, crashed UFOs/alien bodies'.

claims.sourceText: The Wilson-Davis notes as published, all fifteen pages, https://documents2.theblackvault.com/casefiles/wilsonleak.pdf
claims.text: The notes attach no rank, service or first name beyond 'Will' to Miller, and his letter carries no rank block, so the 'Cdr. Willard Miller, USN' form used across the podcast corpus is not supported by the document it is drawn from.

edges.label: His letter of 25 April 2002 is addressed to Davis at Warp Drive Metrics
edges.note: Miller's letter of 25 April 2002 is addressed to Davis at Warp Drive Metrics and offers him paid research assistance.

edges.label: Placed with Greer and Mitchell at the April 1997 Pentagon talk
edges.note: The notes place Miller with Greer and Mitchell at the April 1997 Pentagon talk and record that Miller told Greer what Wilson had said.

edges.label: Named on six of the fifteen pages; his own signed letter is two of them
edges.note: Miller is named on six of the notes' fifteen pages and his own signed letter is bound in as two of them.

edges.label: The private two hour conversation of April 1997, as the notes record it
edges.note: The notes record a private two hour conversation between Miller and Wilson in April 1997 and Wilson's later anger that Miller repeated it.

edges.label: His letter of 25 April 2002 is on United States Navy letterhead
edges.note: Miller's letter is on United States Navy letterhead and Wilson's complaint in the notes is framed in terms of trust among Navy officers, though no rank is stated anywhere in the document.
